To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concentration of the acceptors responsible for the yellow band in GaN is (2.5 +/- 0.3) x 10(17) cm-3.
the acceptor concentration in the YL band of GaN can be determined from the saturation of the Yl intensity at high exciation power density.

(i) the acceptor concentration in the YL band in GaN is about 2.5×1016 cm-3, (ii) the YL intensity increases linearly up to a critical excitation power density of about 0.5 W/cm2 and then it saturates, and (iii) the saturation of the Y L intensity is due to gradual saturation of acceptor states at different distances from sample surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the determination of acceptor concentration from photoluminesence and its application to the determination of concentration of acceptors responsible for YL band.
the determination of acceptor concentration and the nature of deep and shallow defects in GaN.
the study of deep and shallow impurities in GaN and their role in optical properties of this material.

the YL in undoped GaN is due to a deep acceptor with a concentration of about 1017 cm-3, and the acceptor concentration in n-type doped GaN with a donor concentration of 5x1018 cm-3 is about 1016 cm-3.
the YL band is related to a deep acceptor, which is not a native defect in GaN.
the YL band at about 540 nm is due to recombination of electrons with holes localized on acceptors in the band gap, which are most likely carbon atoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the YL band in GaN is due to the radiative recombination of electrons in the conduction band with the holes in the acceptor level at about 0.3 eV from the top of the valence band.
